To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of a high Tg salt to an amorphous drug can enhance the physical stability, but this is opposed by the hygroscopicity of the composite system.

amorphous composite materials of salt and acid forms of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) can be prepared by co-processing, and the ratio of salt and acid affects the glass transition temperature and hygroscopicity of the composite.
The physical stability and hygroscopicity of amorphous composite salt/acid systems can be tuned by optimising the salt/acid ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formulation of amorphous systems with improved stability and reduced hygroscopicity.
the development of novel amorphous salt/drug composite formulations with enhanced stability and reduced hygroscopicity, compared with the pure amorphous forms.
developing new amorphous pharmaceutical materials with improved stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the salt/acid ratio of 1:1 is the best option in terms of physical stability and water uptake.
the amorphous composite of sulfathiazoles with a 1:2 ratio of sulfathiazol:sodium sulfathiazol, with a Tg of 60°C, is the most stable system with the least hygroscopicity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amorphous salt of sulfathiazol is more stable than the pure drug, and the composite system is a promising way to obtain a stable amorphous formulation with low hygroscopicity.
we have developed an amorphous composite system with improved physical stability and reduced hygroscopicity compared to both the salt and the drug alone.
amorphous composite materials can be designed to improve the physical and chemical stability and to reduce the hygroscopicity of amorphous drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical stability of the amorphous systems can be tuned by adjusting the ratio of the salt/acid components.
the ratio of salt to drug in amorphous composites can be tuned to achieve the desired properties.
the water uptake mechanism within amorphous composite materials depends on the ratio of the components, and this should be considered when designing formulations.
